footprint.symmetry: approximate bilateral symmetry along the long axis (towers at opposite ends, repetitive floor bands)

repeated_patterns: Main rectangular block: four repeating floor bands; each floor band has a strip of narrow windows set in sandstone with a wooden accent strip above and stonebrick trim between floors.
raw_elements: continuous narrow horizontal windows on each floor (repeated bands)
two tall corner towers with small square windows and overhanging capped platforms
stepped layered red-tile gabled roof with white eaves
white block low perimeter border and vertical white entrance posts
stonebrick vertical corner trims and banding between floors
raw_hints: Main rectangular block: four repeating floor bands; each floor band has a strip of narrow windows set in sandstone with a wooden accent strip above and stonebrick trim between floors.
Roofs: create a symmetrical stepped gable roof using red brick stairs (or similar) with white eaves (quartz or slab) forming a visible lip.

Towers: place two tall 3-4 block wide towers at opposite ends, with darker stonebrick vertical edges and a lighter sandstone face; add small square windows vertically spaced; top with an overhanging flat platform of layered slabs and a small cap block (glowstone?)
Base: surround the building with a single-layer white block curb spaced one block from walls; ground is flattened dirt/terracotta.
Chamfer the front-right corner by stepping the wall inward on each floor to match the visible angled corner profile.
rebuild_intent.summary: A rectangular multi-story institutional-style building with a stepped red-tiled gabled roof, four regular floors of window bands, horizontal stone/wood banding, and two tall corner towers with overhanging platform caps. The structure sits on a low white-block border/curbstone and is surrounded by cleared ground.
